findings.title: Cache key uses Python hash() which is randomized per process
findings.body: Line 27 builds cache_key with hash(tuple(sorted(snuba_params.project_ids))). Python's hash() for tuples is salted per process (PYTHONHASHSEED), so the same project set maps to different keys in different workers, defeating the cache, and can be negative/collide. Use a deterministic hash (e.g. hashlib) or joined IDs. Consequence is cache misses across hosts and potential cross-key collisions causing wrong eligibility.

findings.title: 60s cached allowlist eligibility returns stale counts
findings.body: is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects caches _are_all_projects_error_upsampled for 60 seconds keyed only by org+projects. If the allowlist changes, queries within the window apply (or skip) sum(sample_weight) incorrectly, over- or under-counting by 1/sample_rate (e.g. 10x). invalidate_upsampling_cache is defined but never called in the diff, so there is no invalidation path. Eligibility must not be cached across requests or must be versioned with the option.

findings.title: Upsampling check uses outer dataset instead of scoped_dataset
findings.body: Inside _get_event_stats the code calls is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects(snuba_params, organization, dataset, request) with the outer closure dataset, not the scoped_dataset argument. The dashboard-split factory below calls _get_event_stats with discover vs scoped_dataset for the same request, so the eligibility decision is made for the wrong dataset. Consequence is upsampling applied (or skipped) for the wrong store, producing wrong timeseries values.

findings.title: Error-query detection misses !event.type:transaction errors-only queries
findings.body: _is_error_focused_query only returns True when the raw query string contains event.type:error. The caller in organization_events_stats.py builds errors-only split queries as (query) AND !event.type:transaction, which contain no event.type:error and therefore return False. Those errors-only queries will skip the upsampled_count transform and under-count by the sample factor, while empty-query discover requests are also mishandled. String matching cannot replace proper query AST parsing.

findings.title: upsampled_count sum(sample_weight) mishandles NULLs and truncates
findings.body: The new SnQLFunction does toInt64(sum(sample_weight)) with no null handling. Backfilled, unsampled, or mixed events have NULL/missing sample_weight, so sum can be NULL or under-count, and toInt64 truncates fractional weights (e.g. 1/0.3) instead of rounding. The comment assumes sample_weight always exists for allowlisted projects, which is false during rollout. Consequence is NULL buckets or systematically low error counts.

findings.title: Test factory unconditionally overwrites sample_rate without validation
findings.body: _set_sample_rate_from_error_sampling does if client_sample_rate: normalized_data[sample_rate] = float(client_sample_rate) with bare except: pass. It clobbers any real sample_rate already set on the event, accepts out-of-range/NaN/Inf values (only float() conversion checked), and treats 0 as absent. Consequence is test (and any reused helper) events get a corrupt sample_rate that changes sample_weight calculation and hides production null-handling bugs.
